_History:_

* _21/10/2026 --- v1.0 -- Initial publication_

# Summary

On 20 October 2026, the PHP foundation announced an upcoming security release addressing two critical vulnerabilities in PHP that could lead to remote code execution, according to other leaks [1,2,3].

At this time, no technical details have been made public. CERT-EU advises organisations to prepare for **immediate patching of affected assets**. Where immediate patching is not feasible, organisations should **consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is available**.

The PHP team has scheduled the release for 21 October 2026 at 14:00 UTC [1].

# Technical Details

No technical details are currently available for **CVE-2026-109618** and **CVE-2026-109619**, apart from their CVSS scores of 9.2, which indicate the potential for unauthenticated remote code execution [1].

# Affected Products

These vulnerabilities could affect all PHP versions from PHP 5 onwards [2]. 

# Recommendations

CERT-EU strongly recommends identifying PHP-based applications and preparing to **patch as soon as fixed versions become available**. Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should **consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix can be applied**.
